title: Dynamics of random recurrent neural networks: colored noise and sublinear activations
authors: German Mato, Facundo Rigatuso, Gonzalo Torroba
abstract: We study the dynamics of recurrent neural networks with random couplings, sublinear odd activation functions, and temporally correlated noise. Using large N methods, we determine stationary correlations and distinguish the loss of local linear stability from the onset of chaos, characterized by a positive largest Lyapunov exponent. These thresholds delimit an intermediate regime in which local instability coexists with asymptotic stability under a common noise history. Their separation depends on both the noise correlation time and the asymptotic growth of the activation function. We show that internal noise with any finite correlation time cuts off the divergence of the network's intrinsic correlation time tau_corr at the edge of chaos; it exhibits a critical scaling tau_{corr,max} propto 1/sqrt{D_0}, where D_0 is the integrated noise strength. Static random input instead produces coincident thresholds and a divergent correlation time. We also calculate the frequency-dependent participation dimension from a four-point correlation function. Its zero-frequency value is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the network correlation time, predicting a smooth minimum at the weak-noise chaos threshold. Numerical simulations support the large-network predictions and reveal appreciable finite-size effects.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the dynamics of random recurrent neural networks subjected to colored noise and sublinear activations. Using large N methods, the authors distinguish between local instability and chaos, finding that internal noise critically limits the network's correlation time at the edge of chaos. This work advances the understanding of stability boundaries in complex, disordered dynamical systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex dynamics of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) characterized by random couplings, sublinear activation functions, and the influence of temporally correlated noise.
main_result: The analysis distinguishes two thresholds—local linear instability and chaos—showing that internal noise with finite correlation time cuts off the divergence of the intrinsic correlation time at the edge of chaos.
method: The research employs large N methods (mean-field theory) to derive self-consistent equations for correlation functions, complemented by chaos diagnostics like the largest Lyapunov exponent.
model_or_system: The model is an RNN governed by a Langevin equation involving quenched random couplings (W_ij), a sublinear activation function f(phi), and dynamical colored noise (xi_i(t)).
key_observables: Largest Lyapunov exponent, intrinsic correlation time (tau_corr), and frequency-dependent participation dimension.
important_parameters: Noise correlation time, integrated noise strength (D_0), and the coupling strength parameter (lambda).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-N limit and assumes the use of a smooth family of sublinear activation functions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the disappearance of separated activity lobes and show the nonmonotonic dependence of the leading Principal Component variance fraction (F_1) on network size (N) for various activation exponents (p).
paper_structure: The paper develops theoretical results using large N methods to analyze the dynamics, contrasting the behavior under internal noise versus static input, and concludes with quantitative predictions for correlation time scaling and dimensionality.
why_interesting: The study provides a framework for understanding how noise and disorder interact to define stability boundaries in complex, non-equilibrium dynamical systems, which shares conceptual links with many-body localization and glassy dynamics.
